conviction_note: The company guided Q4 FY26 consolidated core EBITDA up about $40-50m q/q (to roughly $394-404m). That implies adjusted EPS near $2.00-2.10, so the $1.95-2.00 consensus sits inside the guide. The independent series for Jun-Aug cut both ways and roughly cancel: shredded/HMS scrap fell about $10/gt a month, while long-steel prices were steady-to-down in July on weak seasonal demand and imports. The reaction will turn on the Q1 FY27 outlook. There, October scrap is rising (Fastmarkets +6.6% expected) against flat rebar, the West Virginia carrying costs peak, and an expected CO2 credit offsets part of it. p_up is 49 on abs 4.5 and the findings sum to -0.3; the two measurements agree that this is essentially a non-result.
bar: Adjusted EPS consensus $1.95-2.00 for Q4 FY26 (quarter ended 2026-08-31). Sources: Stocktwits $1.95, revenue $2.56B (https://stocktwits.com/symbol/CMC/earnings); AAII $1.99 on 8 analysts (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/507487-what-you-need-to-know-about-commercial-metals-companys-q4-earnings); Benzinga $2.00, revenue $2.54B (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CMC/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet). Zacks is lower at $1.91 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/what-is-zacks-researchs-forecast-for-cmc-fy2026-earnings-2026-07-27/). The company guide is from the Q3 FY26 release and call of 2026-06-25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022444/000002244426000038/cmc-5312026xearningsreleas.htm; https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026): core EBITDA up sequentially by about $40-50m from $353.6m. That is made up of NASG about +$40m ($20m outage absence plus a similar amount from volume and margin), CSG mid-teens growth, Europe ex-CO2 +$3-5m, less the absent $20.4m CO2 credit. Scrap was assumed stable and metal margins were to return to pre-Q3 levels (Q2 was about $623/t, Q3 $610/t). The consensus sits inside the guide-implied range, and the bar is sourced.
positioning_check: Short interest was 6,310,209 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement: about 5.7% of 110.62m shares outstanding, 5.16 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/cmc/short-interest, read 2026-10-14 per the sweep row). That is moderate and not a crowded short. The baseline's 25-delta skew is +9.54 vol points ('downside paid') and put/call OI is 0.39. However, the front-expiry chain has only 495 contracts of total OI and an ATM spread of 133% of mid, so the skew is barely informative. ATM IV of 76.9% with 2 days to expiry implies roughly ±5.7% but is unreliable. Spot is $64.45: -2.1% over 20 days, -22.6% from the 52-week high, +16.4% from the 52-week low. The monthly price table shows a drift from about $68.7 (Jul) to $67.1 (Sep) (https://www.digrin.com/stocks/detail/CMC/price). Peers NUE and STLD sold off on Q3 guides described as lighter than hoped (https://tradersunion.com/news/stocks/show/3390538-steel-dynamics-slides-4-74percent-to/), so sector sentiment into the print is soft. Insider Form 4s since June are all routine: tax withholding on RSU vesting (Doucet, 2026-10-09, 751 sh at $63.10) and director retainer stock (McPherson, 2026-10-01). There are no open-market buys or sells.

findings.finding: US obsolete scrap (shredded and HMS, CMC's main mill feed) fell about $10/gt each month over the summer, with primes sideways. SMU's August settle had shredded at about $417.50/gt and HMS at $362.50, shredded down $5 from July. Management's Q4 guide assumed scrap 'relatively stable', so the rebar-scrap spread got a modest cost tailwind beyond the guide in a quarter where Q3 scrap had risen about $28/t.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-06-25): the metal margin compressed $13/t q/q on scrap +$28 and the EPS was called a slight miss by some sources, yet the stock rose +3.94% (baseline). Metal-margin beats or misses have not mapped cleanly to the reaction. The guide and the outlook dominated.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $1.95-2.00 sits at or slightly below the guide-implied level. If sell-side models had marked scrap lower than the company's 'stable' assumption, consensus would sit above the guide-implied ~$2.05, and it does not. The effect is small: about $10-15/gt on roughly 1.2m tons of melt is about $10-15m of EBITDA, or about $0.07-0.10/share.
findings.independence: SMU August settle data (https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/08/11/smu-scrap-prices-stagnant-in-august/) and SteelOrbis US longs headlines for July ('lower scrap cost', 'scrap softness') (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-prices/steel-prices-market-analyses/longs-and-billet/us). Steel Dynamics' Q3 guide also cites lower scrap costs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm). This finding shares the metal-spread line with finding 2, which is the offsetting selling-price side.

findings.finding: US long-steel and rebar selling prices were 'steady to down' through July on low seasonal demand, bearish sentiment and more Gulf Coast imports, per SteelOrbis weekly headlines (2, 16, 23 and 30 July). ChemAnalyst had rebar -0.94% in the week to 2026-08-07 and flat thereafter. Firming only came from late August and September. Management guided half of NASG's +$40m q/q to 'volume growth and margin expansion' and admitted on the call to market discounting it would not match. Soft July pricing and demand put that half of the bridge (~$20m, about $0.14/share) at risk, either as lost volume or lower realisations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same line as Q3 FY26: there, shipments fell to 750kt (from 798kt) and the stock still rose +3.94%. The negative reactions (-4.69% Mar-26, -3.56% Jan-26) came on quarters with margin or volume shortfalls against the guide (Q2 FY26 EPS $1.16 vs $1.28, per https://stocktwits.com/symbol/CMC/earnings).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.95-2.00 is roughly at the guide, not below it. A market pricing a volume or price shortfall would show consensus clearly under the guide-implied ~$2.05 and a lower revenue bar than $2.54-2.57B. It does not. The 133%-wide option spread means the skew cannot tell us whether this is hedged. The effect is netted against finding 1 (lower scrap): the spread is what matters, so this is the price side only.
findings.independence: ChemAnalyst, 2026-08-20 (https://www.chemanalyst.com/NewsAndDeals/NewsDetails/us-steel-rebar-prices-stay-range-bound-as-buyers-adopt-44010): rebar -0.94% on Aug 7 then flat, July +0.96% m/m, 'increased import availability', 'comfortable distributor inventories'. Management's own discounting comment is in the Q3 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). Against it: SDI says steel demand is solid and customer inventories low (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001022671/000110465926108777/tm2625690d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: Peer guidance issued after CMC last spoke (both 2026-09-17, covering Jul-Sep) points to a firm EAF steel environment. Steel Dynamics guided Q3 EPS to $5.34-5.38, up from $3.69, on 'metal margin expansion', higher realized prices, lower scrap, record shipments, strong order activity and low customer inventories, with non-residential construction leading demand. Nucor guided steel-mills earnings up on higher selling prices. Both stocks traded down on guides seen as lighter than consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean history of CMC reacting to peer read-through. CMC's own outlook lines have driven its moves, e.g. Q3 FY26's strong Q4 outlook coincided with +3.94%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: these releases are public and both peers sold off on them. What may not be priced is the long-products specific angle. SDI's and Nucor's guides are dominated by flat-rolled, and CMC trades about 6% below its July level, which reads as sector de-rating rather than CMC-specific information. The finding is a proxy for CMC's Q1 FY27 tone and is filed small.
findings.independence: Nucor Q3 guide (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/nucor-issues-q3-2026-earnings-guidance-expects-higher-steel-mills-and-steel-products-earnings-1478837.htm; https://www.tikr.com/blog/nucor-stock-estimates-bake-in-a-60-earnings-rebound-but-q3-guidance-just-missed). SteelOrbis September long-steel headlines 'tight rebar supply', 'US rebar prices inch up' (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-prices/steel-prices-market-analyses/longs-and-billet/us). It is a proxy, not a CMC number.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 (Sep-Nov) outlook faces rising scrap against flat rebar. Fastmarkets' 2026-09-30 survey expects October US ferrous scrap up about 6.6% m/m (trend indicator 65.9), and SteelOrbis on 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-08 had long-steel prices 'flat at Q4 start' while markets 'evaluate higher October scrap trade'. Every source found shows no rebar price increase after May 2026. Q1 also carries seasonal volume decline and the West Virginia micro-mill's pre-revenue carrying cost (~$8-10m/quarter, guided to double in Q4). The semiannual Poland CO2 credit (~$20m) returns in Q1 FY27 and partly offsets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CMC has sold off on weak next-quarter outlooks before: fiscal Q4 2023 fell more than 10% intraday when management guided Q1 down on seasonal shipments and North American margin compression (https://www.fool.com/investing/2023/10/12/why-commercial-metals-stock-is-down-big-today). The baseline's -7.26% on 2025-10-16 is the largest of the last seven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: spot is -2.1% over 20 days and the (illiquid) skew pays for downside. If the market had fully discounted a Q1 margin squeeze, the stock would trade near its 52-week low instead of 16% above it, and consensus FY27 numbers would visibly have been cut. The only revision signal found is an undated Barchart headline about downward revisions. Scrap is also the mill's pass-through lever: a rising scrap month usually enables a rebar increase, which caps the size.
findings.independence: SteelOrbis headlines 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-08 (https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-prices/steel-prices-market-analyses/longs-and-billet/us). SMU notes October buyers paying up $20/gt for shredded in Detroit (https://www.steelmarketupdate.com/2026/08/11/smu-scrap-prices-stagnant-in-august/ page sidebar). The West Virginia carrying cost and CO2 timing come from the Q3 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026). Against it: SteelOrbis 2026-09-03 and 2026-09-17 report tight rebar supply and prices inching up.

findings.finding: Capital return capacity is large relative to the pace so far. The 2026-08-05 Investor Day 8-K added $600m of buyback authority (about $717m total, about 10% of a ~$7.1bn market cap), against only $18.9m repurchased in Q3 FY26. FY27 capex is guided about $200m lower as West Virginia spend falls. The 2026-10-13 8-K held the dividend at $0.20, with no raise ahead of the print. The Q4 release will disclose the Jun-Aug repurchase pace and possibly an FY27 capital return framework.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved CMC print where the buyback pace was the line. The Investor Day itself (2026-08-05) did not lift the stock: the price table shows it drifting from $68.7 (Jul) to $67.5 (Aug).
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public and priced. Only the Q4 execution pace is unknown, and with net leverage at 2.1x against a sub-2x target it is more likely modest than aggressive. That is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Dividend 8-K, 2026-10-13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/22444/000002244426000048/cmc-8312026xdividendxex991.htm). Leverage and capex commentary from the Q3 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CMC/Q32026).

outside_window.finding: The West Virginia micro mill reaches saleable product and ramps over about 12 months (250-300kt in FY27), and the FY27 free-cash-flow ramp follows. These are multi-quarter catalysts beyond the first session.
Nucor's Q3 results (2026-10-26) and Steel Dynamics' (2026-10-19) will give long-products detail after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The illiquid skew (+9.5, 'downside paid') and the soft 20-day run-up lean slightly negative. My one negative outlook finding (Q1 scrap squeeze) agrees with them and is therefore partly priced. The reported-quarter findings net to about zero inside the company's own guide, so nothing here argues strongly against the market's mild bearish lean, and p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (finding inside guidance): scrap tailwind cut from +0.6 to +0.4, and July pricing softness from -0.8 to -0.6. Both land inside a guided q/q EBITDA bridge the market was told to expect.
Rule 5 (proxy): peer SDI/NUE read-through cut from +0.4 to +0.3. It is flat-rolled-dominated, CMC has not confirmed it, and it is labelled a proxy in independence.

Rule 7 (skew and short interest): Q1 FY27 scrap squeeze cut from -0.7 to -0.6 because it agrees with the downside skew and is partly priced. Short interest was checked (5.7%, 5.2 DTC, not crowded), so no squeeze cut was applied.
Rule 6 (bar): the bar was verified against three estimate sources agreeing at $1.95-2.00 plus the company's EBITDA guide, so no cap was needed.
Net: the sum is unchanged at -0.3 because the cuts were symmetric. p_up stays at 49 and abs_move_pct at 4.5.
